scenario_text: A government-owned insurance company needs a claims processing portal for rural customers. All requirements have already been documented in a 200-page RFP. The portal must comply with IRDAI regulations. The team has 15 developers, funding is approved for 18 months, and the requirements will not change once signed off.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a claims processing portal accessible to rural customers
requirements.business_justification: Rural customers may have limited access to urban centers and require remote access to submit claims
requirements.assumptions: Rural customers have access to internet and basic digital devices
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal is accessible via mobile and desktop browsers with minimal system requirements
applicable_regulations: IRDAI

requirements.statement: The system shall comply with all IRDAI regulations for insurance claims processing
requirements.business_justification: Non-compliance with IRDAI regulations could result in legal penalties and loss of license
requirements.assumptions: IRDAI regulations are available and up to date
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System passes IRDAI compliance audit and certification
applicable_regulations: IRDAI

requirements.statement: The system shall support offline data entry for claims submission in areas with poor internet connectivity
requirements.business_justification: Rural areas may have intermittent or no internet access, requiring offline functionality for data entry
requirements.assumptions: Users have devices capable of storing data locally and syncing when connectivity is available
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users can submit claims after entering data offline and sync with the system when internet is available
applicable_regulations: The Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations, 2021 (No. 2 of 2021 (K-11020/240/2021/Auth/UIDAI)) [updated 15 Dec 2025]

requirements.statement: The system shall provide multilingual support for rural users who may not be fluent in the primary language
requirements.business_justification: Supporting multiple languages improves usability and ensures all users can understand and interact with the system
requirements.assumptions: The system will support at least the major local languages in the target regions
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system provides user interface and content in at least three major local languages

requirements.statement: The system shall ensure data privacy and security in accordance with applicable data protection laws
requirements.business_justification: Protecting user data is essential to maintain trust and avoid legal consequences
requirements.assumptions: Applicable data protection laws are known and followed
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System passes penetration testing and meets data encryption standards

requirements.statement: The system shall allow users to track the status of their claims in real-time through a dedicated dashboard.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users must see the current status of their claim, including any pending actions, approvals, or rejections, with timestamps for each step.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide users with email and SMS notifications for key claim processing events, such as submission confirmation, approval, and payment disbursement.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users must receive notifications within 5 minutes of the event occurring, with a confirmation log available in the user portal.

requirements.statement: The system shall support the correction or resubmission of incomplete or incorrect claim data by users.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users must be able to view error messages, edit the relevant fields, and resubmit the claim without losing previous data.

requirements.statement: The system shall handle failed external service calls (e.g., payment gateways, third-party verification services) by retrying the operation up to three times with a delay of 10 seconds between attempts.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system must log all failed attempts and notify administrators if the operation fails after three retries.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide administrators with a dashboard to monitor system performance, user activity, and claim processing metrics in real-time.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Administrators must be able to view system uptime, error rates, and claim processing times with filters for date, region, and claim type.
applicable_regulations: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, 2023 §2 (IRDAI/GA&HR/GDL/MISC/88/04/2023) [issued 24 Apr 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall support the configuration of claim processing thresholds and rules by administrators, such as maximum claim amounts per category.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Administrators must be able to define and update thresholds through a secure interface, with changes taking effect immediately and being auditable.

requirements.statement: The system shall store all claim-related data, including user submissions, approvals, and payment records, for a minimum of 10 years.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Data must be archived in a secure, tamper-proof format and be retrievable for audit or legal purposes.

advantages.advantage: Test cases written early, from the requirements
advantages.relevance: This aligns with the need to ensure that the claims processing portal (REQ-001) meets the usability and accessibility needs of rural customers, as defined in the RFP.

advantages.advantage: Defects found at the stage that caused them
advantages.relevance: This supports the requirement for offline data entry (REQ-003) by catching issues early, ensuring that the system can function reliably in areas with poor connectivity.

advantages.advantage: Every requirement traceable to a test
advantages.relevance: This ensures that multilingual support (REQ-004) is fully tested and implemented, meeting the usability needs of rural users who may not be fluent in the primary language.

justifications.gives_up: V-Shaped assumes an existing system is being extended — that is not the case here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: Agile is the most suitable model due to its flexibility and iterative approach, which aligns with the high-priority, high-risk requirements that involve regulatory compliance, usability, and privacy. It allows for continuous stakeholder feedback and adaptation to evolving regulations and user needs.

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: Cyber security incidents reported promptly to RBI
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Cyber Security Framework in Banks §15 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall detect and log cyber security incidents and support reporting them to RBI (and CERT-In) within the mandated timelines.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Insurer's ICT logs, critical and business data stored in India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, 2023 §14 (IRDAI/GA&HR/GDL/MISC/88/04/2023) [issued 24 Apr 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep its ICT infrastructure logs and all critical and business data in India, with logs retained for a rolling 180 days.

risk_register.title: Payment system data stored only in India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Storage of Payment System Data §2 (RBI/2017-18/153 DPSS.CO.OD No.2785/06.08.005/2017-2018) [issued 06 Apr 2018; compliance due 15 Oct 2018])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall store the full end-to-end data of every payment transaction only in systems located in India.

risk_register.title: Personal data breaches notified to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §8(b) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support detection of personal data breaches and notification of each breach to the Data Protection Board and every affected customer in the prescribed form and time.

risk_register.title: Personal data processed only with the data principal's consent (or another lawful ground)
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §4 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall obtain and record the customer's consent for each specified purpose before processing their personal data, and allow the consent to be withdrawn as easily as it was given.

risk_register.title: Suspicious and large cash transactions recorded and reported (STR/CTR)
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 §3 (G.S.R. 444(E)) [consolidated text, as amended])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall flag suspicious transactions and cash transactions above the prescribed threshold, keep their records, and produce suspicious- and cash-transaction reports for the Financial Intelligence Unit.

risk_register.title: A grievance redressal mechanism for customers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services §7 (RBI/2023-24/102) [issued 10 Apr 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall let customers raise complaints and disputes, track them to resolution, and show the contact details of the designated grievance redressal officer.

risk_register.title: Notice to the data principal stating what personal data is collected and why
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §5 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted])

risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall present a notice, before or at the time of collection, stating the personal data collected, the purpose of processing and how the customer can exercise their rights and complain.

risk_register.title: Outsourced or third-party IT services under due diligence, audit rights and an exit plan

risk_register.title: Personal data erased when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is served — unless law requires retention

risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall erase a customer's personal data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served, except where retention is required by law (such as the five-year KYC record retention), and record the basis for any retention.

risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
